newsitem.title: USA: H.F.Ahmanson bids $6 billion for Great Western.
newsitem.headline: H.F.Ahmanson bids $6 billion for Great Western.

text.p: H.F. Ahmanson & Co. said Tuesday that it offered $6 billion to acquire Great Western Financial Corp., a major California banking rival, in a stock deal that would create one of the biggest financial powerhouses in the country.
Ahmanson, the nation's largest thrift, said it offered to swap 1.05 of its shares for each share of Great Western, which is the country's second-largest savings and loan holding company.
A combination of the two companies, which are both based in Los Angeles suburbs, would create a company with about $93 billion in assets, Ahmanson said.
Great Western officials were not immediately available to comment on the deal early Tuesday morning.

Ahmanson said its bid valued Great Western shares at $42.53 each, for a premium of about 24 percent over the stock's closing price Friday. Ahmanson shares closed at $40.50 last week while Great Western closed at $34.25.
The company also said it expected "immediate and substantial" benefits to its earnings per share from the transaction, but it gave no specific figures.
It said the transaction would save it more than $400 million in pre-tax costs by 1999.
Ahmanson said the cost-savings, coupled with planned stock repurchases, would add 5 percent to its cash earnings per share in 1997, 15 percent in 1998 and 26 percent in 1999.
It added that the deal would be accounted for as a purchase and would be tax-free. The transaction, however, is subject to approval by both companies' boards, and well as regulatory bodies.

Ahmanson also said it would nominate three individuals to Great Western's board -- Lawrence Del Santo, chairman of the Vons Cos., Robert Gelber, former partner of the law firm Gibson, Dunn & Crutcher, and Wolfgang Schoellkopf, former vice chairman of First Fidelity Bancorp.
Great Western, which is based in Chatsworth, Calif., has about 14,300 employees and 1,150 offices, mostly in California and Florida.
Ahmanson, with headquarters in Irwindale, Calif., owns several savings banks, including two big thrifts in New York state, with more than 450 branch offices.
